subject: Television & Streaming
title: Television and the Civil Rights Movement
description: One-minute skill: Television and the Civil Rights Movement.

hook.text: In 1963, television cameras broadcast police using fire hoses and attack dogs on Black children in Birmingham, Alabama.

buildup.text: The footage shocked white Americans who had no idea how violent segregation was.

discovery.text: Martin Luther King Jr. understood television's power.

twist.text: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 passed partly because television made ignoring injustice impossible.

climax.text: Television became the civil rights movement's most powerful ally—not by advocating, but by simply showing the truth.

punchline.text: The camera didn't take a side. It didn't need to.

quiz.question: How did television contribute to the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964?
options: Broadcast footage of segregation's violence made it impossible for the public to ignore
